title: Particle verbs III: the idiomatic ones
title_target: Vad går din uppsats egentligen ut på?
goal: Understand and use the particle verbs whose meaning you can't guess from their parts — the ones that make everyday Swedish sound natural.
bekal: *komma fram till*, *gå ut på*, *stå ut med*, *slå igenom*, *ställa upp*, *ta itu med*, *hålla med*
where *inte*, adverbs and objects go in a particle verb sentence
families of particle verbs built on one verb: *ställa upp / in / till*, *komma fram till / an på / emellan*
wave: Go back to Unit 5: reread its first dialogue and underline every *ju*, *väl* and *nog*. This unit's dialogues are full of them too — notice how they slip in between the verb and the particle: *Det har jag **ju** alltid sagt*, *Ni har **ju** jobbat med det*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Fika med Oskar
dialogs.intro: Oskar is in Stockholm for a weekend, and he and Dian meet at a café near the university. He hasn't seen her since she started her thesis, and he wants to hear everything — especially how Göteborg comes out of it.

lines.text: Nå, berätta nu. Vad går din uppsats egentligen ut på?

lines.literal: well, tell now. what goes your essay actually out on?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Den går ut på att jämföra hur Stockholm och Göteborg planerar för grönytor.
lines.id: It's about comparing how Stockholm and Göteborg plan for green spaces.
lines.literal: it goes out on to compare how Stockholm and Göteborg plan for green-surfaces

lines.text: Och vad har du kommit fram till hittills?

notes: **Vad går den ut på?** — *gå ut på* means "to be about, to consist in, to aim at". It is the natural way to ask what a book, film, job or plan is about: *Vad går jobbet ut på?* What follows is either a noun or an *att*-clause: *Den går ut på **att** jämföra…* Stress: **VAHD gohr den ÜT poh**.

**Kommit fram till** — *komma fram till* is literally "come forward to" (and can still mean that: *Vi kom fram till Uppsala klockan tre*). In discussions it means "to reach a conclusion": *Vad kom ni fram till?* What did you conclude? It is far more common than the formal *dra slutsatsen att*.

**Står du ut med** — *stå ut med* = "to stand, to put up with, to tolerate". Usually negative or in questions: *Jag står inte ut med honom.* *Hur står du ut?* It also works without an object: *Jag står inte ut längre!* (I can't take it any more!)

**Höll jag på att ge upp** — from Unit 3: *hålla på att* + infinitive in the past often means "nearly, almost": *Jag höll på att ramla* (I almost fell). Context decides between "was in the middle of" and "nearly".

**Ställer alltid upp** — *ställa upp* has a whole range of meanings, but the most Swedish one is "to be there for someone, to help out": *Tack för att du ställde upp!* It can also mean "to take part" (*ställa upp i ett lopp*, in a race) and "to agree to" (*ställa upp på en intervju*). **Köra fast** — "to get stuck", from a car stuck in snow or mud.

**Ta itu med** — "to deal with, to tackle, to get to grips with" a task or problem. *Itu* is an old form meaning "in two", so the image is breaking something in half to deal with it. Say **tah ee-TÜ meh**, stress on *-tu*. **Hålla med** (to agree) is the other must-have from this dialogue: *Jag håller med dig/henne/om det.* **Se till att** = "to make sure that".

grammars.title: Seven particle verbs you can't guess
body: In Svenska 102 and 103 most particle verbs had a meaning you could partly see through: *stänga av* (turn off), *ta upp* (pick up). The verbs in this unit are different: their meaning has drifted far from the parts. Learn each one as a single word, with its preposition.

head: Verb
Literally
Meaning
Example
rows: Vi kom fram till att planen var för dyr.
to be about, to aim at
Spelet går ut på att samla poäng.
to put up with, to stand
Jag står inte ut med bullret.
to break through, to become popular
Hon slog igenom med sin första roman.
to help out; to take part; to agree to
Han ställer alltid upp för sina vänner.
Nu måste vi ta itu med disken.
Jag håller med dig om det.

after: In all of them, the **particle carries the stress** and the verb is said lightly: *stå ÜT med*, *slå ee-YEH-nom*, *hålla MEHD*. If you stress the verb instead, Swedes may hear a literal meaning: *STÅ ut* sounds like "stand outside".

grammars.title: Where do inte, adverbs and objects go?
body: The particle is glued to the end of the verb phrase. Sentence adverbs (*inte*, *alltid*, *ju*, *aldrig*) go **between** the finite verb and the particle in a main clause, and **before** the whole verb in a subordinate clause (BIFF).

head: Type
Example
rows: Ibland står jag **inte** ut med henne.
Jag kan **inte** stå ut med det.
Ta itu med **det** nu! · Hon ställde upp på **den**.

after: In Swedish the particle normally comes **before** an object, even a pronoun: *räkna ut det*, *ta upp den*. Norwegian and Danish often do the opposite (*regne det ut*), which is a good shibboleth if you ever hear a Scandinavian speaking Swedish.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — En intervju med Ahmad
dialogs.intro: Ahmad, Dian's old corridor neighbor, now works as an engineer at an energy company. Dian wants to interview him for her thesis chapter on solar panels on apartment buildings, so she calls him one evening.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ahmad, skulle du kunna ställa upp på en intervju till min uppsats?
lines.id: Ahmad, would you be willing to do an interview for my thesis?
lines.literal: Ahmad, should you can place up on an interview to my essay?

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Klart jag ställer upp. Vad gäller det?
lines.id: Of course I will. What's it about?
lines.literal: clear I place up. what concerns it?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Solceller på flerfamiljshus. Ni har ju jobbat med det i flera år.
lines.id: Solar panels on apartment buildings. You've been working on that for years.
lines.literal: sun-cells on multi-family-houses. you have ju worked with it in several years

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Ja, det slog igenom på allvar för fem år sedan, när elpriserna steg.
lines.id: Yes, it really took off five years ago, when electricity prices went up.

lines.text: Precis. Jag vill veta varför vissa bostadsrättsföreningar ändå tackar nej.

lines.text: Det betyder att ingenting blir av. Ett annat problem är att lönsamheten är svår att räkna ut.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Kan du gå igenom en sådan kalkyl med mig?

lines.text: Visst. Men jag måste sätta mig in i de nya reglerna först — de ändrades i januari.

notes: **Klart jag ställer upp** — *klart* (short for *det är klart att*) is a casual "of course". Note that what follows has main-clause word order but no inversion: *Klart jag gör!* Similar: *Självklart!*, *Absolut!*

**Slog igenom på allvar** — *slå igenom* (to break through) is used for artists who become famous, but also for ideas, technologies and trends: *Elbilen slog igenom 2020.* **På allvar** = "seriously, for real".

**En bostadsrättsförening** (BRF) — most Swedish city apartments are owned through a housing cooperative: you buy the right to live in the flat (*bostadsrätt*), and the association (*förening*), run by an elected board (*styrelse*), owns the building. Every decision about the roof — including solar panels — goes through the board.

**Det kommer an på** = "it depends on", a common alternative to *det beror på*. Stress: **deh kom-mer AHN poh**. **Rinna ut i sanden** ("run out into the sand") is a fixed image for plans that slowly come to nothing — English "fizzle out" or "peter out".

**Blir av** — *bli av* (to happen, to come off) is mostly used with *inte* or *ingenting*: *Resan blev aldrig av* (The trip never happened). **Räkna ut** = to work out, to calculate. **Gå igenom** = to go through, to review.

**Sätta sig in i** — a reflexive particle verb meaning "to get to know, to familiarize oneself with": *Jag måste sätta mig in i reglerna.* The reflexive pronoun sits between verb and particle. **Komma emellan** = "to come up, to get in the way": *Om inget kommer emellan ses vi på torsdag.*

grammars.title: One verb, many particles
body: The most efficient way to learn idiomatic particle verbs is in families around the same basic verb. The basic verb gives you nothing; the particle gives you everything.

head: Verb + particle
Meaning
Example
rows: Tack för att du ställde upp!
Vi kom fram till ett beslut.
Låten slog igenom i hela Norden.
to look up; to break up
Slå upp ordet! · De har slagit upp förlovningen.

after: Note the difference between **hålla med** (to share an opinion: *Jag håller med dig*), **komma överens** (to reach agreement or get along: *Vi kom överens om datumet*) and **gå med på** (to accept a proposal, often reluctantly: *Till slut gick han med på det*). English uses "agree" for all three.

blocks.text: Many of these verbs still have a literal meaning alongside the idiomatic one. Context — and often the presence of a preposition and an object — tells you which is meant.

head: Verb
Literal
Idiomatic
rows: Vi kom fram till ett svar. (concluded)
Hon ställer alltid upp. (is there for people)
Skylten står ut från väggen. (sticks out)
Jag står inte ut! (can't stand it)
Bilen körde fast i snön. (got stuck)
Jag har kört fast i kapitel tre. (am stuck)

blocks.title: How to learn them
items: Always learn the preposition that goes with the verb: not *stå ut*, but *stå ut **med** något*.
Write one sentence about your own life for each verb — personal sentences stick.
Say them aloud with the stress on the particle: *hålla MEHD*, *ta ee-TÜ med*, *gå ÜT på*.

blocks.text: Particle verbs are the backbone of spoken Swedish. In formal writing, many have a one-word equivalent — often a prefixed verb or a loan from Latin. Knowing both lets you move between registers (more on this in Unit 14).
Notice *beräkna* from Unit 6 (*arbetet beräknas påbörjas*): officialese often uses the fused form where speech uses the particle verb — *räkna ut* in the kitchen, *beräkna* in the report.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Svenska 103, Unit 7
items: There you met separable vs fused pairs: *gå under* (sink, perish) / *undergå* (undergo), *ta upp* / *uppta*.
Add today's pairs: *räkna ut* / *beräkna*, *ta emot* / *mottaga*, *stå ut* / *uthärda*.
Rule of thumb: the separated form is everyday and concrete; the fused form is formal or abstract.
